title: MLOps Engineer
description: A production-focused roadmap for MLOps: ML foundations, experiment tracking, data/model versioning, CI/CD, serving, monitoring, and cloud deployment. This roadmap emphasizes practical skills and industry best practices for building, deploying, and maintaining robust machine learning systems in production.

tree.name: Fundamentals for MLOps
tree.description: Build a strong base in software engineering, machine learning principles, foundational systems knowledge, and data engineering concepts required for MLOps.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (Shell, Git)

children.name: Software Engineering Essentials
children.description: Master Python programming, project structuring, dependency management (Poetry, pip-tools), unit testing (pytest), structured logging, and version control with Git.

children.name: Linux & Command Line Interface Basics
children.description: Understand fundamental Linux commands, shell scripting, environment variables, process management, and file system navigation essential for automation and server interaction.

children.name: Networking & Distributed Systems Basics
children.description: Learn about TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, Load Balancing concepts, and fundamental principles of distributed systems like fault tolerance and consistency, critical for understanding deployed ML services.

children.name: Machine Learning Core Concepts & System Design
children.description: Grasp the ML lifecycle, data types, model training, evaluation metrics, overfitting, underfitting, bias, ethics, basic model explainability (e.g., LIME, SHAP), and principles of designing scalable and reliable ML systems.

children.name: Data Engineering Fundamentals
children.description: Understand data storage (SQL, NoSQL, object storage), ETL/ELT concepts, data warehousing basics, data quality, and schema management for robust ML data pipelines.

children.name: Introduction to DevOps Principles
children.description: Familiarize yourself with core DevOps concepts like continuous integration, continuous delivery, infrastructure as code, configuration management, and site reliability engineering (SRE).

tree.name: Experimentation, Data & Model Management
tree.description: Implement robust systems for tracking experiments, versioning datasets, and managing model artifacts to ensure reproducibility, auditability, and collaboration across the ML lifecycle.

resources.title: Complete End-to-End Deep Learning Project with MLflow, DVC, and Deployment (Krish Naik)

children.name: Experiment Tracking Principles
children.description: Understand the necessity of logging experiment runs, parameters, metrics, code versions, data versions, and model artifacts for effective iteration, debugging, and comparison. Learn about reproducibility in ML.

children.name: Data Versioning & Management
children.description: Learn strategies for versioning datasets, managing data lineage, handling large files efficiently, and ensuring data integrity for reproducible training and validation.

children.name: Model Artifact & Registry Management
children.description: Manage model binaries, associated pre-processing logic, model metadata, and promote models through different lifecycle stages (staging, production) using a model registry.

resources.title: Versioning and Managing ML Models in Production

children.name: Tool Deep Dive: MLflow
children.description: Practical application of MLflow for experiment tracking, model logging, artifact storage, and managing a comprehensive model registry, including advanced features like MLflow Projects.

children.name: Tool Deep Dive: DVC
children.description: Practical application of DVC for versioning data and large model files, integrating with Git, and building reproducible ML pipelines that track dependencies and outputs.

children.name: Practice Lab: Reproducible ML Workflow
children.description: Implement a fully reproducible ML workflow, versioning data with DVC, tracking experiments with MLflow, and comparing model versions end-to-end. Focus on making the entire process auditable and shareable.

tree.name: CI/CD and Model Serving
tree.description: Automate the build, test, and deployment process for ML models, ensuring robust, scalable, and secure serving infrastructure with proper integration and continuous delivery practices.

resources.title: MLOps Dockerized Flask CI/CD with GitHub Actions (Krish Naik)

children.name: Containerization with Docker
children.description: Master Docker for packaging ML models and their dependencies into portable containers, including Dockerfile best practices, multi-stage builds, efficient image layering, and Docker Compose for local orchestration.

children.name: Model Serving Patterns & Prediction APIs
children.description: Explore different model serving architectures (REST, gRPC, batch, real-time), build efficient prediction APIs with frameworks like FastAPI or Flask, implement health checks, handle concurrency, and manage model dependencies.

resources.title: Building Scalable ML Model Serving Infrastructure

children.name: CI/CD for Machine Learning Systems
children.description: Design and implement robust CI/CD pipelines specific to ML, including automated code testing (unit, integration), data validation, model validation, performance testing, and artifact promotion across environments.

children.name: Tool Deep Dive: GitHub Actions for MLOps
children.description: Configure and manage CI/CD pipelines using GitHub Actions for automating ML workflows, from code commit, data validation, model training, testing, to model deployment and release.

children.name: Model Validation & Testing in CI
children.description: Implement robust testing for ML models including data quality checks, statistical model performance tests, fairness assessments, explainability tests, and integration tests within CI pipelines to prevent regressions.

children.name: ML Deployment Strategies
children.description: Understand and implement various deployment strategies like Blue/Green, Canary releases, Shadow Deployment, and A/B testing for ML models in production environments to minimize risk and enable gradual rollouts.

children.name: API Gateways & Load Balancing
children.description: Learn to configure API Gateways and Load Balancers for exposing ML models, managing traffic, enforcing security, rate limiting, and ensuring high availability and scalability of prediction services.

tree.name: Cloud Deployment, Orchestration & Monitoring
tree.description: Operate and scale ML services in cloud environments using container orchestration, ensuring high availability, robust monitoring, proactive issue resolution, cost efficiency, and strong security posture.

children.name: Cloud Platform Fundamentals (AWS/GCP/Azure)
children.description: Understand core cloud services (compute - EC2/GCE/VMs, storage - S3/GCS/Blob, networking - VPC/VNet, IAM, serverless functions - Lambda/Cloud Functions), regional deployments, and cost management principles relevant to ML workloads.

children.name: Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
children.description: Master IaC principles and tools like Terraform or AWS CloudFormation/GCP Deployment Manager for provisioning and managing cloud resources (VMs, networks, databases, Kubernetes clusters) in a version-controlled and automated manner.

children.name: Container Orchestration with Kubernetes
children.description: Deploy and manage containerized ML services using Kubernetes, covering fundamental concepts (Pods, Deployments, Services, Ingress, Persistent Volumes), autoscaling, Helm charts for package management, and interacting with managed Kubernetes services (EKS, GKE, AKS).

children.name: Managed ML Platforms & Services
children.description: Explore and utilize managed ML platforms like AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, or Azure ML for streamlined development, training, tuning, and deployment of ML models, including managed inference endpoints and batch prediction services.

children.name: Feature Stores & Online/Offline Serving
children.description: Understand the architecture and benefits of feature stores (e.g., Feast, Tecton) for managing, transforming, and serving features consistently across training and inference, including online and offline feature serving patterns.

resources.title: Feast: An Open Source Feature Store

children.name: Observability: Metrics, Logging & Tracing
children.description: Implement comprehensive observability for ML systems using structured logging, metrics collection (Prometheus, Grafana), and distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry) for monitoring system health, performance, and troubleshooting complex issues.

children.name: ML Monitoring & Drift Detection
children.description: Set up monitoring for data drift, concept drift, model performance degradation, data quality issues, anomalous behavior, and explainability in production ML models to ensure their continued quality, reliability, and fairness.

children.name: ML Pipeline Orchestration (Airflow/Kubeflow)
children.description: Orchestrate complex, multi-stage ML pipelines using tools like Apache Airflow or Kubeflow Pipelines for scheduling, dependency management, error handling, resource allocation, and reproducibility of entire ML workflows.

children.name: Security & Governance in MLOps
children.description: Address critical security concerns in ML systems, including data privacy (encryption, anonymization), model access control, compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2), responsible AI principles, MLOps auditing, and ethical considerations.

children.name: Capstone Project: End-to-End Production ML Pipeline
children.description: Build and deploy an end-to-end ML pipeline on a cloud platform, incorporating all MLOps best practices: data/model versioning, CI/CD, scalable serving with Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, and comprehensive monitoring and drift detection.
